title: On‑Prem vs VPC migration swing analysis & bundle playbook
content:
Purpose:
This working spreadsheet-style playbook captures a compact set of migration 'swing' scenarios for customers considering a move from hosted/Dedicated to either fully on-prem or VPC private deployments. It focuses on a) unit cost sensitivity to utilization and instance mix, b) license + support bundle tradeoffs, and c) clear operator recommendations for bundle configurations by customer archetype.

High-level approach and assumptions (quick):
- Time horizon: 36 months (default) for CAPEX amortization and breakeven windows.
- Workloads modeled: chat generation (token-heavy) and embeddings (high QPS, lower token per call).
- GPU types: A100-80GB equivalent (onprem) vs cX-n. We normalize to a throughput metric: tokens/sec-per-GPU.
- Utilization bands: low (20%), mid (45%), high (75%) sustained.
- Currency: USD, all costs annualized unless noted.
- Licensing: two primary licence types used in model: "per-GPU-instance" annual license, and "throughput" license (per-1M-tokens).
- Support tiers: Basic, Standard, Enterprise (different SLAs and incident response hours).
- Bursting: VPC customers can buy burst credits; we model burst premium = +25% effective unit cost for tokens served by burst pool.

Sheet layout (tabs imagined):
1) scenario-summary (this doc): compact rows with scenario key metrics and top-line recommendation.
2) raw-calc: full line-by-line calc, assumption cells, and formula cells.
3) sensitivity: tornado charts and two-way tables for utilization vs license model.
4) bundle-library: description and price points for each license/support SKU.
5) ops-checklist: steps and handoffs for migrations and post-migration knobs.

Column definitions (scenario-summary):
- scenario_id: short label (e.g., S1-HIGH-ONPREM)
- deployment_type: onprem | vpc
- primary_gpu: A100-80GB | cX-n
- annual_tokens: integer (tokens/year)
- avg_utilization: pct (20%/45%/75%)
- capex_one_time: USD
- annual_opex_infra: USD (power/rack/network)**
- license_annual: USD (annual license line)
content_2:
- support_annual: USD
- effective_unit_cost_per_1M_tokens: formula cell (see below)
- breakeven_months: months to payback relative to hosted baseline
- notes_recs: short text summary

Key formulas (text version for reviewers):
- total_3yr_cost = capex_one_time + (annual_opex_infra + license_annual + support_annual) * 3
- effective_unit_cost_per_1M_tokens = IF(annual_tokens>0, total_3yr_cost / (annual_tokens / 1e6 * 3), "N/A")
- monthly_runrate_equivalent = (annual_opex_infra + license_annual + support_annual) / 12 + capex_one_time/36
- breakeven_months_vs_hosted = IF(hosted_annual_cost>0, 12 * (capex_one_time + (annual_opex_infra + license_annual + support_annual) - hosted_annual_cost) / hosted_annual_cost, "calc")

Sample scenario rows (representative numbers for illustration only):
- S1-MID-ONPREM: deployment_type:onprem; primary_gpu:A100-80GB; annual_tokens:12,000,000,000; avg_utilization:45%; capex_one_time:1,200,000; annual_opex_infra:180,000; license_annual:240,000; support_annual:60,000; => effective_unit_cost_per_1M_tokens approx $18–22 (depends on capex amortization policy). Notes: good fit if customer can sustain steady util >40% and wants full data control.
- S2-HIGH-VPC: deployment_type: vpc; primary_gpu:cX-n; annual_tokens:30,000,000,000; avg_utilization:75%; capex_one_time:0; annual_opex_infra:480,000 (cloud infra committed); license_annual:360,000; support_annual:120,000; burst_premium_est: +10% of tokens; => unit cost per 1M tokens approx $9–12. Notes: VPC favored for high sustained throughput if customer prefers Opex model and avoids capex.
- S3-LOW-ONPREM: deployment_type:onprem; annual_tokens:1,200,000,000; avg_utilization:20%; capex_one_time:700,000; annual_opex_infra:120,000; license_annual:120,000; support_annual:36,000; => unit cost per 1M tokens > $100. Notes: on-prem not recommended unless there are non-financial drivers.

License + support bundle tradeoffs (recommendation matrix):
- SMB/light users (< 3B tokens/yr): recommend throughput-license (per-1M tokens) + Basic support. Rationale: avoids capex and high fixed support fees. Offer a step-down pricing for tokens >X to incentivize committed volume.
- Mid-market (3B–15B tokens/yr): mixed model. If >45% utilization projected: recommend Dedicated on VPC with per-GPU license + Standard support. Include optional burst credits for seasonal spikes.
- Enterprise (>15B tokens/yr or strict data residency): recommend on-prem with Enterprise bundle if customer requires air-gapped or strict data-control. Include longer-term financing to smooth capex. Negotiate support SLOs into contract (4hr P1).

Bundle play actions (operator-focused):
- Bundle A (Economy): throughput-license @ $X/1M tokens + Basic support. Target: PoC, startups.
- Bundle B (Balanced): per-GPU annual license + Standard support + 50% burst credits. Target: scale SaaS teams wanting stable latency.
- Bundle C (Enterprise): per-GPU license (multi-year discount) + Enterprise support (onsite/phone oncall) + optional managed updates. Target: regulated customers.

Migration swing analysis notes (unique framing):
- \"Swing\" means the delta in unit economics when utilization, license model, or support tier changes. For each scenario run a 3x2 grid: utilization band (20/45/75) x license model (throughput vs per-instance). That matrix almost always reveals a cross-over utilization point where per-instance licensing becomes cheaper than throughput licensing — capture that point per-customer.
- Sensitivity drivers, ranked: 1) Utilization, 2) Annual tokens, 3) License structure, 4) Support tier, 5) Capex financing cost.

Operational checklist (pre-migration):
- Confirm realistic utilization profile with customer: instrument current hosted calls for 30 days (ENG-1429).
- Capture token distribution by route: embeddings vs chat vs longform.
- Confirm networking egress and dedicated interconnect needs (network opex often undercounted).
- Decide amortization schedule (36 vs 60 months) and include financing options.
- Add compliance addendum if on-premement requires audit logging or HSM integration.

Deployment knobs and cost optimizations:
- Autoscaler config: configure narrower instance classes to keep utilization above cross-over point.
- Prefix/KV cache sizing: reduce token generation by eliminating repeat prefix recomputation; estimate savings by modeling cache hit rate at 10%/30%/50%.
- Quantization recommendations: if model tolerates INT4 quantization, expect 20–35% lower GPU footprint; re-run scenario with reduced capex + lower license baseline.
- Batching windows and latency SLO: small increase in tail latency permitted for 10–15% batching can halve unit cost in some workloads.

Sample quick-sensitivity (text):
- Example: S1 baseline (45% util) unit cost = $20/1M tokens. If utilization falls to 30% unit cost -> $28/1M. If license model switches to throughput at current volumes unit cost -> $26/1M. If quantization reduces GPU count by 30% unit cost -> $14/1M.

Negotiation playbook (sales-facing):
- Always present both the \"steady-state\" and \"seasonal-peak\" pricing. Include burst credits as an explicit line item.
- Offer a 12–18 month hybrid: start on VPC with committed throughput discount, then convert to on-prem capex package with credit for prior payments if surface-level ROI is positive after 12 months.
- Include a service onboarding credit for customers who sign Enterprise bundle in 60 days.

Open questions / TODOs (for modeling team):
- Add per-route token mix scenarios (embeddings-heavy vs chat-heavy) into raw-calc. (Owner: Marco, due: 2026-03-05, ticket: ENG-2143).
- Integrate real list prices for cX-n family (cloud) and vendor quotes for A100 replacements (onprem).
- Build violin plot of unit cost distribution across 100 Monte Carlo draws on utilization (sigma=0.12).

Notes on presentation: keep this spreadsheet lean (1–2 pages visible for exec summary), push full raw calculation to separate hidden tab for audit. This doc should be treated as internal sales enablement (do not share vendor pricing line items externally without legal review).
